Migrating split-sex projection inputs

Current spmR requires input format 2 for new ADMB projections. Version 0.4.3 embeds its declarations as comments in each species file by default. This guide uses synthetic data to show the change from legacy split-sex files to explicit recruitment and population-weight declarations. Validation runs whenever this vignette is built; native execution in the final worked example is enabled explicitly.

What changes in the input files

Keep the positional layout of spm.dat. In each split-sex species file (for example, stock.prj), insert wt_M immediately after wt_F. The current engine does not read or require tacpar.dat. Use write_spm_metadata() to append a versioned comment block with the declarations for each stock.

  • Declare the basis of the complete historical recruitment series: "total" for both sexes combined or "per_sex" for either sex under a 50:50 recruitment ratio. Pooled-sex inputs require "total".
  • Supply female and male population weight-at-age vectors in the metadata. Each vector carries its age labels. The positional wt_F and wt_M vectors supply female and male spawning weights, and wt_gear_F and wt_gear_M supply catch weights. Female spawning weight continues to determine SSB.
  • Keep the initial female and male abundance vectors in the species file. The recruitment-basis declaration applies to historical recruitment; it leaves these sex-specific initial vectors unchanged.
  • Use N_scalar = 1. Convert existing scaled data to the declared units before creating metadata. Update values as needed while preserving field order.

Keep population-weight vectors in the versioned comment block. The positional wt_M vector supplies spawning weights. Adding another positional field can shift subsequent fields. The current native engine reads the appended comment block directly, preserving the existing positional field order. The R runner validates the declarations and checks executable compatibility. Recompile the current inst/admb/spm.tpl to use embedded inputs directly.

A reproducible synthetic input folder

The following small example represents two sexes, one fishery, and three ages. All abundance values are fish, all weights are kg, and catch and biomass are kg. Replace these synthetic values with assessment inputs for an actual projection.

projection_dir <- tempfile("spmr-split-sex-")
dir.create(projection_dir)
ages <- 1:3

# Comments identify fields and make the new split-sex order explicit.
write_fields <- function(fields, path) {
  lines <- unlist(Map(function(name, values) {
    c(paste("#", name), paste(values, collapse = " "))
  }, names(fields), fields), use.names = FALSE)
  writeLines(lines, path)
}

write_fields(list(
  run_name = "synthetic_split_sex", Tier = 3, nalts = 1, alt_list = 5,
  TAC_ABC = 1, SrType = 2, Rec_Gen = 1, Fmsy_F35 = 1, Rec_Cond = 0,
  Write_Big = 1, npro = 3, nsims = 100, styr = 2026, nyrs_catch_in = 1,
  nspp = 1, OY_min = 0, OY_max = 2000000, spp_file_name = "stock.prj",
  ABC_Multiplier = 1, N_scalar = 1, Alt4_SPR = 0.6, ntacspp = 1,
  tac_ind = 1, Obs_Catch = c(2026, 0)
), file.path(projection_dir, "spm.dat"))

write_fields(list(
  spname = "synthetic_split_sex", SSL_spp = 0, Const_Buffer = 0,
  ngear = 1, nsexes = 2, avg_5yrF = 0.2, FABC_Adj = 1,
  SPR_abc = 0.4, SPR_ofl = 0.35, spawnmo = 4, nages = 3, Frat = 1,
  M_F = rep(0.2, 3), M_M = rep(0.2, 3),
  pmature_F = c(0, 0.5, 1), pmature_M = c(0, 0.5, 1),
  wt_F = c(0.1, 0.25, 0.5),
  wt_M = c(0.08, 0.2, 0.4),
  wt_gear_F = c(0.2, 0.4, 0.6), wt_gear_M = c(0.15, 0.3, 0.45),
  sel_F = c(0.1, 0.5, 1), sel_M = c(0.1, 0.5, 1),
  n0_F = c(100, 200, 300), n0_M = c(100, 180, 250),
  nrec = 4, R = c(80, 100, 120, 100), SSB = rep(1000, 4)
), file.path(projection_dir, "stock.prj"))

Add explicit recruitment and population weights

Here the historical values 80, 100, 120, 100 represent total recruitment. Population weights differ from the spawning and fishery weights above.

species <- list(list(
  file = "stock.prj",
  recruitment_basis = "total",
  ages = ages,
  units = list(abundance = "fish", weight = "kg", biomass = "kg"),
  population_weights = list(
    female = list(ages = ages, values = c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3)),
    male = list(ages = ages, values = c(0.08, 0.16, 0.24))
  )
))

write_spm_metadata(projection_dir, species)
inputs <- validate_spm_inputs(projection_dir)
stopifnot(inputs$format_version == 2L)
inputs$resolved_species[[1]]

write_spm_metadata() embeds version-2 declarations in stock.prj and validates the complete input folder. Weight vectors must contain one finite, strictly positive value per age. Age labels must be consecutive, ascending, nonnegative integers and match the species file’s age count and abundance ordering, including its final plus group. The validator checks labels and dimensions; the author establishes that the original assessment values follow the declared order.

Supported abundance/weight/biomass combinations are fish/kg/kg, thousand_fish/kg/t, and million_fish/kg/thousand_t. The metadata checks the declaration; it performs no unit conversion. All stocks in a run must share abundance and biomass units.

The appended block for this synthetic stock is:

# SPMR_INPUT_V2 2 1
# stock.prj 2 3 1 1 1 1 0
# 1 2 3
# 0.1 0.2 0.3
# 0.08 0.16 0.24
# END_SPMR_INPUT_V2

The versioned header identifies one stock. Its record gives the filename, sex count, age count, recruitment basis, abundance/weight/biomass unit codes, and male-weight substitution code. The final three rows contain ages, female population weights, and male population weights. Use the R writer to build and validate the block from named declarations.

Existing JSON workflows

The default metadata = NULL reads embedded declarations first. When no species file has a block, it falls back to spm_metadata.json. To select a JSON file explicitly, use the same metadata argument throughout:

write_spm_metadata(projection_dir, species, metadata = "spm_metadata.json")
validate_spm_inputs(projection_dir, metadata = "spm_metadata.json")
runSPM(projection_dir, run = TRUE, metadata = "spm_metadata.json")

The R runner prepares embedded declarations for current engines and generates the legacy spm_input_v2.dat sidecar for older format-2 engines. The current native engine accepts that sidecar when embedded declarations are absent.

How recruitment is normalized

For split-sex inputs, a per-sex history of 40, 50, 60, 50 represents the same total history as this example. The engine doubles the complete per-sex history before calculating its arithmetic mean, harmonic mean, variability, recruitment distribution, or stock–recruitment inputs. It then allocates each projected total equally to the two sexes once. Doubling only a fitted mean would leave other calculations on a different basis.

The calculation below illustrates the normalization; the native regression suite checks the engine’s recruitment moments, reference points, and trajectories.

total_history <- c(80, 100, 120, 100)
per_sex_history <- c(40, 50, 60, 50)
stopifnot(identical(total_history, 2 * per_sex_history))
c(
  arithmetic_mean = mean(total_history),
  harmonic_mean = 1 / mean(1 / total_history)
)
arithmetic_mean   harmonic_mean
      100.00000        97.95918

Choose the basis from the assessment’s recruitment definition. If the input history is already total recruitment, label it "total". Metadata describes the stored series; setting "per_sex" on total values would double them. Initial abundance at the youngest age is already supplied in n0_F and n0_M.

Missing male weights and explicit substitutes

A split-sex input with missing male population weights stops before execution, including when strict = FALSE. That argument controls unknown metadata fields; the scientific checks remain active.

missing_male <- species
missing_male[[1]]$population_weights$male <- NULL
male_error <- tryCatch(
  write_spm_metadata(projection_dir, missing_male),
  error = function(e) conditionMessage(e)
)
stopifnot(grepl("missing male population", male_error, fixed = TRUE))
cat(male_error)
metadata species 1 (stock.prj): missing male population weight-at-age vector; supply it or explicitly declare male_population_substitute.

An author may explicitly select "female_population" (use female population weights for males) or "mean_male_fishery" (use the unweighted arithmetic mean of male fishery weights across fleets, at each age). Both choices produce a warning and enter the run record. Record the scientific reason for using a substitute in the assessment and compare its effect on biomass. Supply either male weights or a substitute selection.

substituted <- missing_male
substituted[[1]]$male_population_substitute <- "female_population"
write_spm_metadata(projection_dir, substituted)
Warning: metadata species 1 (stock.prj): male population weights use declared
female_population.
# Restore the measured/synthetic sex-specific vectors for the main example.
write_spm_metadata(projection_dir, species)

Verify the starting year and total biomass

The supplied initial abundance must represent the beginning of styr in spm.dat (2026 here). If the assessment state is from the preceding year, advance survival and ageing, accumulate the plus group, and explicitly choose the youngest-age recruitment for the starting year before writing the files. The metadata declaration alone performs none of these boundary calculations.

Total biomass at the beginning of the year is the sum over ages of female abundance times female population weight plus male abundance times male population weight. For this synthetic input:

stock <- inputs$species[[1]]
weights <- inputs$resolved_species[[1]]$population_weights
initial_biomass_kg <- sum(stock$n0_F * weights$female +
  stock$n0_M * weights$male)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(initial_biomass_kg, 236.8)))
initial_biomass_kg
[1] 236.8

Holding abundance and population weights fixed while changing fishery weights preserves this first-year biomass. Fishery weights can change catch and the fishing mortality required to attain a catch, affecting later trajectories. Spawning biomass uses female abundance, maturity, spawning weights, and survival to spawning time.

In detailed output, Year = t biomass uses beginning-of-year abundance in year t, while Rec is the draw entering the youngest age in year t + 1. Ntot reports mature abundance. Use all ages and population weights for the independent total-biomass check above.

Run and retain the evidence

Build inst/admb/spm.tpl with ADMB 13.0 or newer, then place the resulting spm (or spm.exe on Windows) in the projection folder or on PATH. The runner checks the executable’s -spmr-capabilities response before execution.

The template includes its format-2 reader and compiles on its own; there is no separate spmr_input_v2.hpp dependency. The example helpers can compile the installed template with admb on PATH, or a compiler selected by SPMR_ADMB. After updating the source checkout, reinstall spmR to refresh that template. The current engine reports both SPMR_INPUT_FORMAT=2 and SPMR_INLINE_INPUT=1. With the embedded blocks in place, a standalone run needs spm.dat and its species files. Older format-2 engines require the sidecar generated by the R runner.

The run record includes executable and input SHA-256 hashes, declared units, recruitment basis, resolved population weights, substitutions, and output hashes. Each attempt has a record in spm_run_history/; the last successful record is retained separately. Archive the input folder and results together.

Supported new runs use TAC_ABC = 1, Rec_Gen = 1 (historical recruitment distribution) or 2 (stock–recruitment fit), and N_scalar = 1. Fitted runs require a maximum gradient below 1e-4 and a positive-definite Hessian. Auxiliary recruitment modes 3 and 4, TAC fitting, and new experimental RTMB projections require further implementation.

Read archived output with runSPM(..., run = FALSE) without changing its inputs. Adding metadata leaves those historical results as they were; produce new results in a separate folder, review recruitment, biomass and reference points, and then update assessment tables.

Worked example: 2020 Greenland turbot

The repository includes a documented conversion of the 2020 Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands Greenland turbot projection. The assessment treated this as a Tier 3a stock and projected ages 1–30, with age 30 as the plus group. The example retains the archived two-sex species input and writes all converted inputs and outputs to a temporary directory. It is a source-checkout example; clone the spmR repository before running the code below.

The helper embeds its validated declarations as comments in the generated species file. The current native engine reads that file and spm.dat directly; the R runner supplies a sidecar when using an older format-2 executable.

The conversion declares total recruitment in thousand_fish, weights in kg, and biomass in t. The archived female spawning weights are reused as female population weights to preserve legacy biomass. No independent male population-weight vector was archived, so the example explicitly records mean_male_fishery; this is a reproducibility substitute, not a new biological estimate.

# Locate the example both when Quarto starts in vignettes/ and when it starts at
# the package root.
gt20_candidates <- c(
  file.path("..", "examples", "gt20"),
  file.path("examples", "gt20")
)
gt20_source_dir <- gt20_candidates[file.exists(file.path(
  gt20_candidates, "run_spmR_split_sex.R"
))][1]
if (is.na(gt20_source_dir)) {
  stop("Clone the spmR source repository to run the GT20 worked example.")
}
gt20_source_dir <- normalizePath(gt20_source_dir, mustWork = TRUE)
source(file.path(gt20_source_dir, "run_spmR_split_sex.R"), local = TRUE)

# Input conversion and validation run in every build. Set SPMR_RUN_GT20=true to
# opt in to native execution; the pkgdown workflow sets it after compiling the
# pinned engine.
gt20_run_native <- identical(
  tolower(Sys.getenv("SPMR_RUN_GT20", unset = "false")), "true"
)
gt20_executable <- ""
gt20_admb <- ""
if (gt20_run_native) {
  gt20_executable <- Sys.getenv(
    "SPMR_EXECUTABLE",
    unset = Sys.getenv("SPMR_TEST_EXE", unset = "")
  )
  if (!nzchar(gt20_executable)) gt20_executable <- unname(Sys.which("spm"))
  gt20_admb <- Sys.getenv("SPMR_ADMB", unset = "")
  if (!nzchar(gt20_admb)) gt20_admb <- unname(Sys.which("admb"))
  if (!nzchar(gt20_executable) && !nzchar(gt20_admb)) {
    stop("SPMR_RUN_GT20=true but no SPM executable or ADMB compiler was found.")
  }
}

gt20 <- run_gt20_projection(
  source_dir = gt20_source_dir,
  run_dir = tempfile("spmr-gt20-vignette-"),
  executable = gt20_executable,
  admb = gt20_admb,
  build = TRUE,
  run = gt20_run_native
)
Warning: GT20 uses declared mean_male_fishery population weights for males.
Completed GT20 projection in /tmp/Rtmp7XR2sm/spmr-gt20-vignette-1b4b3877a1df; starting biomass = 92104.6 t.
data.frame(
  metric = "Beginning-of-2020 total biomass (t)",
  value = round(gt20$initial_biomass, 1)
)
                               metric   value
1 Beginning-of-2020 total biomass (t) 92104.6

With SPMR_RUN_GT20=true, the same evaluated chunk runs all seven alternatives and verifies 14,000 rows (100 simulations over 20 years). The published site build supplies a pinned ADMB 13.2 engine and displays this concise alternative-1 summary and its provenance record.

if (gt20_run_native) {
  print(gt20$summary[
    gt20$summary$Alt == 1 & gt20$summary$Year <= 2022,
    c("Alt", "Year", "SSB", "Catch", "ABC", "OFL")
  ])
  data.frame(
    executable_sha256 = gt20$provenance$executable_sha256,
    recruitment_basis = gt20$provenance$species[[1]]$recruitment_basis
  )
} else {
  cat(paste(
    "Format-2 inputs validated; set SPMR_RUN_GT20=true to run the native",
    "projection."
  ))
}

The example reproduces beginning-of-2020 total biomass of 92,104.6 t. For alternative 1, mean 2021 SSB is 51,913.9 t and ABC is 7,326.4 t, matching the published projection after rounding. The complete source is examples/gt20/run_spmR_split_sex.R.

The separate 2026 Greenland turbot example preserves the revised export and audits its unresolved definitions. Its 47 recruitment values and 45 SSB values block staging until matching source histories are supplied. Diagnostic population weights are fishery-weight proxies requiring an explicit choice and separate scientific review.
